newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South Africa sends plane for Zaire's Kabila.
newsitem.headline: South Africa sends plane for Zaire's Kabila.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela, bidding to rescue Zairean peace talks, sent a jet to Cabinda in Angola on Thursday to fetch rebel leader Laurent Kabila for talks in Cape Town, an official said.

Presidential spokesman Parks Mankahlana said Deputy President Thabo Mbeki would remain in Pointe Noire, Congo, where the talks were to have taken place on Wednesday, to maintain contact with Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko.

Mankahlana said Mandela would brief Kabila, who refused at the last minute on Wednesday to leave the Angolan enclave of Cabinda and meet Mobutu on a South African ship, on his late-night talks with the Zairean president.
"In our view the talks are not derailed. Kabila has not said that he will not talk, he has merely raised concerns about his security," he said.
Mankahlana said South Africa was studying a lengthy response from Mobutu to a two-page South African proposal for a transition to democracy.
He said Kabila had yet to submit his response to the plan, which has been endorsed by most African and Western leaders.
